card.law_is_about: Continuing federal funding for the Deutschlandticket in 2026.
card.they_want: Remove the expiry of the discounted Deutschlandticket Job offer.
card.they_claim: 48 million people are employed subject to social-insurance contributions.
card.the_problem: The official figures available before the submission put that category at about 34.77 million, rather than 48 million.

correction: The BA September 2025 report, published on 30 September before the 1 October submission, estimated 34,768,800 employees subject to social-insurance contributions in July 2025. This is about 13.2 million below the claimed 48 million. Its broader all-employed category was 45.95 million in August, which is a different population; the case does not identify where the author obtained 48 million.
effect: Reduces the stated size of the named employee target group supporting continuation of the discounted job ticket. It does not proportionally reduce actual or prospective ticket sales.
limits: Minor category/size correction only. The job ticket may also be available to workers outside the stated social-insurance category; 34.77 million is not a demonstrated cap on eligibility or demand. The BA estimate was provisional and lagged the submission by two months. A typographical error or loose shorthand for a broader working population is plausible. No financial-impact calculation or policy rejection follows, and no intent is inferred.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the count substantially overstates the specifically named category, but is an auxiliary scale argument, not a calculated uptake, budget, or benefit estimate. The large remaining group and independent planning-certainty reasons still support discussion of the request.
direction_explanation: True for the stated argument: a larger employee target group strengthens the scale rationale for removing the job-ticket expiry. This does not establish that actual eligible users or policy benefits were overstated by the same amount.
context_and_alternatives: Read all four pages of the official written submission. The count immediately follows the job-ticket expiry-removal request; other paragraphs separately discuss general funding, administration, and apprentices.

The official hearing page identifies this statement with 6 October 2025 and BT21/1495. The body is dated 1 October 2025; the committee stamp has an inconsistent 2026 year, treated as an administrative header error, not an additional author finding.
Read exact draft cover and operative pages 5–7: funding is extended for 2026. The job-ticket continuation is a requested accompanying policy, not falsely described as already enacted by that draft.

The BA total is a people count at workplace, not a count of all jobs. Its 7.66 million marginally paid workers includes 3.47 million secondary jobs, so adding all marginal jobs to social-insurance employees would double-count people and still not validate the stated category.

Searched the full 27-page oral transcript for the number and job-ticket qualifications; read targeted VDV opening and job-ticket discussion on pages 6 and 16. The witness gives independent planning-certainty and employer-demand reasons. No oral repetition or explicit correction of 48 million was found; this is not an author response to this screen.
